Review copy — The Memory Experiment, Twice: a Team Retro and a Personal-Framework Field Report

"Just vibe code it" has become a normal thing to hear in engineering. Over about six weeks this fall, a small group of us at Mezmo built an agent memory service mostly with coding agents, took it from nothing to a working service in our dev environment, and got a successful demo out of it. Whether it makes later agent investigations better, we haven't measured yet; more on that to come. This piece is what that taught me about speed, review and breakage. I don't have the final answer. I want to start a conversation with the engineers who will have to live with whatever we settle on, and the sceptics most of all.

Where the pressure comes from

The push comes from the whole industry, and mostly from the top. Shopify's CEO told staff that reflexive AI usage is a baseline expectation. Coinbase's CEO fired engineers who didn't onboard to AI tools within a week, and set a goal of more than half its code being AI-written.

So both camps have a point: in these numbers, output goes up, and so do review load and instability.

Where I stand

The shift I expect is from "prevent every break" to break fast, detect fast, fix fast. DORA's own guidance says "speed and stability are not tradeoffs". The incident record backs the mechanics. Google Cloud's June 2025 outage report traced the failure to a code path that "did not have appropriate error handling nor was it feature flag protected." CrowdStrike's root cause analysis landed on staged rollout with rollback.

Risks and open questions

  • The tiers only work if "experiment" really means throwaway. An experiment that touches production credentials or shared data is high blast radius, whatever we call it.
  • Detection costs something. Flags and canaries carry their own debt, and I haven't found a good public number for what they cost a small team.
  • Would AI review have caught what ours missed? The blind review experiment above should give a first answer, though it won't settle how deep review should go. I'll write it up whatever it shows.
